next_round_constraints: Keep delay_weeks in {0,1}; avoid 2-week delays for delayed_I on this series.
Prefer simpler structures (SEIR baseline) unless adding a compartment is paired with a clear, constrained observation mapping; avoid SEIRS for now.
If using SEIHR, restrict observation_map to a single compartment (H only or I only); avoid composite I+H observations.
Limit complexity increases: only one change from the current best at a time (either structure OR observation_map OR delay), not multiple simultaneously.
Prioritize rolling stability: propose templates expected to be robust across split points (e.g., fewer free degrees of freedom in observation mapping).
observed_failure_modes: Delay sensitivity: delayed_I with 2-week delay shows markedly worse rolling behavior than 1-week, suggesting forecasts are brittle to lag choice and may be misaligning peak timing.

Over-parameterization/structure mismatch: adding SEIRS (waning) or SEIHR with composite observation (I+H) degrades rolling performance, indicating extra compartments/mixtures are not supported by the short training window and increase instability.

Observation-map mismatch for hospitalization-rate target: mapping to I (even delayed) can fit but may be indirectly capturing hospitalization dynamics; direct H mapping did not improve rolling, implying the H process/scale may be mis-specified or too flexible without additional constraints.

Multi-split generalization weakness: several specs show substantially worse rolling mean errors than single validation, consistent with peakiness/high-rate series causing overfit to the held-out segment timing/shape.
feedback.proposer_instruction: Center proposals around the current best (SEIR, obs=delayed_I, delay=1) and explore only small, controlled variations: (a) test SEIR with delay=0 vs delay=1 to check whether explicit delay is necessary; (b) if proposing SEIHR, use obs=H with tight/implicit linkage to I (no mixtures) and keep delay=0 or 1 only; (c) avoid SEIRS and avoid I+H observation mixtures. Aim for templates that preserve peak timing alignment and reduce rolling brittleness rather than adding compartments.
